chunks: 3669 - Al-Husayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ narrated, saying:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, “What is permissible for a man from the wealth of his child?” He said, “His sustenance, without extravagance, if he is compelled to it.”

He said: So I said to him, “Then what about the saying of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, ‘You and your wealth belong to your father’?” He said, “Rather, he brought his father to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, this is my father, and he has wronged me regarding my inheritance from my mother.’ Then the father informed him that he had spent it on him and on himself, so he said, ‘You and your wealth belong to your father.’ And the man had nothing with him. So would the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله imprison a father for a son?”
ai.seo_question: What is permissible for a father to take from his child’s wealth in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that a father may take from his child’s wealth only what suffices for his sustenance, without extravagance, when he is in need. It also clarifies that the Prophetic statement, “You and your wealth belong to your father,” was tied to a specific case and is not an unrestricted permission for a father to appropriate his child’s property.
